description: Hi! I'm Harish, creator of Star Dust. I'm passionate about Astrophysics and Cosmology. As a CSE student, I use my software development and data analysis skills to make complex scientific data interactive and accessible to everyone.
summary:
SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive, AI-powered web platform that transforms NASA's complex infrared observations into an accessible and engaging scientific exploration experience. Our project enables students, researchers, educators, and astronomy enthusiasts to explore genuine SPHEREx data without requiring advanced programming knowledge or specialized astronomical software.

The platform integrates five major features: "Sky Explorer" for visualizing authentic FITS images, "Epoch Comparison" for analyzing observations captured at different times, "Candidate Investigator" for examining detector quality and potential signals, "Spectral Explorer" for studying infrared flux measurements, and a "Gemini-powered Research Assistant" for understanding astronomical concepts and scientific data.

Developed using Next.js, React, Python, FastAPI, and scientific computing libraries, our solution combines interactive visualization, celestial coordinate alignment, observation metadata, quality validation, and evidence-based analysis.

SPHEREx Explorer addresses the challenge of making space science more accessible while maintaining scientific accuracy and transparency. By connecting real NASA observations with intuitive tools and AI-assisted explanations, our platform encourages curiosity, strengthens scientific literacy, supports meaningful investigation, and inspires future generations to explore the universe through authentic astronomical evidence and discovery.
details:
SPHEREx Explorer

1. Project Overview

SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive, AI-assisted astronomical exploration platform developed to make NASA's SPHEREx infrared observations accessible, understandable, and scientifically meaningful.

NASA's SPHEREx mission surveys the sky using infrared spectroscopy to investigate the history of the universe, galaxy evolution, and the distribution of ingredients essential for life. However, scientific observations are often stored in complex FITS (Flexible Image Transport System) files that require specialized software and technical knowledge to interpret.

Our team, Star Dust, developed SPHEREx Explorer to bridge this gap by transforming authentic astronomical observations into an intuitive, browser-based scientific workspace.

Rather than simply displaying beautiful space images, our application allows users to explore real scientific measurements, compare observations, investigate data quality, understand infrared spectra, and learn through AI-assisted explanations.

2. How Our Project Works

SPHEREx Explorer combines five integrated scientific workspaces.

Sky Explorer — Interactive Infrared Visualization

Users can explore genuine NASA SPHEREx FITS observations through an interactive image viewer. The application supports astronomical target selection, image visualization, contrast adjustments, color mapping, celestial-coordinate inspection, and scientific metadata exploration.

Our curated dataset includes 7 astronomical targets and 41 cataloged observation products, featuring galaxies and variable stars such as M101, M51, M33, NGC 253, Mira, Delta Cephei, and Algol.

This feature allows users to investigate actual scientific observations rather than relying on simulated or decorative space imagery.

Epoch Comparison — Investigating Changes Over Time

The Epoch Comparison workspace enables users to compare observations of the same astronomical target captured at different times.

The application uses celestial World Coordinate System (WCS) information to align compatible images and provides interactive comparison methods, including side-by-side, swipe, and blink views.

When scientific requirements are satisfied, users can examine difference and significance maps. The platform also evaluates observation compatibility, image overlap, detector quality, and available uncertainty information.

Importantly, the application does not automatically classify visible differences as astronomical discoveries. It highlights scientific limitations and supports evidence-based interpretation.

Candidate Investigator — Scientific Quality Assessment

Astronomical observations can contain detector artifacts, invalid pixels, saturation effects, and measurement limitations.

Our Candidate Investigator helps users understand these issues by presenting observation screening results, detector-quality flags, and scientific reliability information.

This encourages users to evaluate the quality of evidence before drawing conclusions about potential astronomical signals.

Spectral Explorer — Understanding Infrared Measurements

The Spectral Explorer enables users to investigate available spectrophotometric measurements associated with the M101 galaxy.

It presents infrared flux-density measurements, uncertainties, detector-band information, and observation identifiers through interactive scientific visualizations.

This helps users understand how astronomical measurements vary across the available infrared samples while preserving the relationship between measurements and their original observations.

AI Research Assistant — Learning Through Natural Language

We integrated the Google Gemini API to provide an AI-assisted research experience.

Users can ask questions about astronomical targets, SPHEREx observations, infrared astronomy, and scientific terminology.

The assistant uses relevant project context to make complex concepts easier to understand, helping students and beginners engage with authentic astronomical data.

AI-generated explanations are treated as educational assistance rather than independent proof of scientific discoveries.

3. Technologies and Tools Used

Our project uses a modern full-stack architecture supported by scientific computing tools.

Frontend Development

  • Next.js 16
  • React 19
  • TypeScript
  • Tailwind CSS

Backend Development

  • Python 3.12
  • FastAPI
  • Uvicorn

Scientific Data Processing

  • Astropy for FITS processing and astronomical coordinate systems
  • NumPy for numerical calculations
  • SciPy for scientific analysis
  • reproject for astronomical image alignment

Artificial Intelligence

  • Google Gemini API for context-aware scientific explanations

Data Sources

  • Genuine NASA SPHEREx FITS observations
  • NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA)

Development and Deployment

  • Git and GitHub for source-code management
  • Vercel for frontend deployment
  • Render for backend deployment

The platform operates through a web browser and does not require specialized astronomical hardware.

4. Creativity and Innovation

The main innovation of SPHEREx Explorer is its integration of authentic scientific observations, interactive visualization, scientific validation, and AI-assisted learning into a single accessible platform.

Our project is creative in several ways:

Real Scientific Data: Unlike applications that rely entirely on simulated imagery, SPHEREx Explorer works with genuine NASA observation products.

Unified Scientific Workflow: Users can move between image exploration, multi-epoch comparison, quality investigation, spectral analysis, and AI explanations without switching between multiple specialized applications.

Evidence-Driven Exploration: The platform preserves observation identities, processing information, and scientific limitations, allowing users to understand how conclusions are supported.

Interactive Learning: Complex astronomical concepts become easier to explore through visual controls, scientific charts, and natural-language explanations.

Responsible Scientific Interpretation: Our system communicates uncertainty and data-quality limitations rather than presenting every visual difference as a confirmed discovery.

5. Benefits and Intended Impact

SPHEREx Explorer aims to reduce the gap between professional astronomical research tools and public scientific engagement.

For Students: It provides hands-on exposure to genuine NASA observations, helping students learn about infrared astronomy, astronomical imaging, and scientific reasoning.

For Educators: It offers an interactive resource for demonstrating real scientific data, measurement uncertainty, and observational analysis.

For Astronomy Enthusiasts: It makes complex space observations accessible through a familiar web interface.

For Scientific Literacy: It encourages evidence-based thinking by showing why data quality, coordinate alignment, and uncertainty matter when interpreting astronomical measurements.

Our intended impact is to make authentic space science more inclusive, engaging, and understandable while inspiring future generations to explore astronomy, astrophysics, and scientific computing.

6. Challenges and Design Considerations

During development, our team considered several important technical and scientific factors.

Scientific Accuracy: We prioritized authentic observation data, correct metadata interpretation, and transparent scientific limitations.

Data Quality: We incorporated detector-quality screening and observation compatibility checks to reduce misleading results.

Image Alignment: Comparing astronomical observations requires celestial-coordinate registration rather than simple pixel-by-pixel comparison.

Performance: Scientific FITS processing can be computationally demanding, so we separated backend analysis from frontend visualization.

Accessibility: We designed the interface to support users who may not have experience with Python, FITS files, or astronomical analysis software.

AI Reliability: We positioned Gemini as an explanatory assistant, not as a replacement for verified scientific measurements.

Reproducibility: We emphasized traceable observation identities and exportable analysis information.

7. Future Scope

We plan to expand SPHEREx Explorer as additional suitable observations and verified scientific measurements become available.

Potential future improvements include:

  • Supporting more astronomical targets and observation products.
  • Expanding spectral exploration to additional objects.
  • Introducing guided scientific investigations for educational use.
  • Improving interactive comparison and visualization tools.
  • Enhancing reproducible scientific reports and analysis workflows.
  • Providing more accessible explanations of astronomical measurements and uncertainty.

Conclusion

SPHEREx Explorer transforms complex NASA infrared observations into an interactive, evidence-driven scientific experience.

By combining authentic astronomical data, modern web technologies, scientific Python processing, and AI-assisted learning, our project makes infrared astronomy more accessible while preserving the accuracy and transparency essential to scientific investigation.

Our vision is simple: Explore the Infrared Sky. Understand the Evidence. Inspire Discovery.
